provenance.note: RENAME-ONLY re-validation over the blessed 4.6.13 line: 5.0.0 is the package-rename release and is statistically identical to 4.6.13. Generated by drivers/mice/{mice_gate,compare_r_reproduce}.py against a PyPI-installed pystatistics==5.0.0 (detect_install_source()==pypi). CPU-vs-R fidelity and CPU+MPS gate legs were RE-RUN fresh on the Mac (throwaway PyPI 5.0.0 venv, R mice 3.19.0); the deterministic fp64 CPU legs reproduce 4.6.13 byte-for-byte, MPS-fp32 aggregate metrics (Rubin coverage 0.945, no separation collapse) reproduce within the already-tolerated single-precision stochastic tier. The CUDA leg (runs/mice_gate_cuda.json) is CARRIED FORWARD from the 4.6.13 Forge run unchanged: the GPU kernels are byte-identical across the 5.0.0 rename, so no re-measurement was warranted; the live MPS leg confirms the GPU code path behaves. Driver edits were validation-side PooledSolution field renames only (dfcom->df_complete, .se->.standard_errors, .ci_low/.ci_high->.ci_lower/.ci_upper); no library change. No R16 showstopper; the version floor is not raised by mice.

studies.title: fp32 gate + Rubin coverage + separation + default (CUDA, authoritative, carry-forward)
studies.note: numeric_gate: pooled slopes cover the known truth for cpu/gpu/gpu_fp64; the large single-rep pooled-SE spread is RNG noise (gpu_fp64, same precision as cpu, shows it too). coverage: 40-rep Rubin coverage ~0.92-0.955 across backends (target 0.95), mean-SE within ~2%. separation: a perfectly-separated binary column imputes to ~0.49 class-1, no silent collapse (discrete fits fp64 on CUDA). default: mice(data, seed=0) works.
